Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada model prarelasi menggunakan data spesifik tugas tertentu.
Model pembanding standar yang digunakan untuk mengukur keunggulan metode baru.

background.en: Speech emotion recognition in low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited annotated data, speaker variability, and the multimodal nature of emotional expression. Addressing these issues in languages like Urdu is critical for developing inclusive affective computing systems, yet existing approaches struggle with speaker bias and data scarcity.
background.id: *Speech emotion recognition* dalam bahasa yang berstatus *low-resource* tetap menjadi tantangan karena terbatasnya data beranotasi, variabilitas penutur, dan sifat ekspresi emosi yang multimodal. Mengatasi masalah ini pada bahasa seperti Urdu sangat penting untuk pengembangan sistem komputasi afektif yang inklusif, namun pendekatan yang ada masih terkendala oleh bias penutur dan kelangkaan data.

contributions.en: This paper repositions established components including wav2vec 2.0, XLM-R, cross-modal attention, and multitask affective modeling into a unified framework. This combination is jointly validated across speaker-independent, cross-lingual zero-shot, and attribution-faithfulness generalization for Urdu, representing a combination not jointly reported in prior Urdu speech emotion recognition work.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memposisikan ulang komponen mapan yang mencakup wav2vec 2.0, XLM-R, *cross-modal attention*, dan *multitask affective modeling* ke dalam satu kerangka kerja terpadu. Kombinasi ini divalidasi secara bersamaan pada generalisasi *speaker-independent*, *cross-lingual zero-shot*, dan *attribution-faithfulness* untuk bahasa Urdu, yang mewakili kombinasi yang belum pernah dilaporkan secara bersamaan pada penelitian *speech emotion recognition* bahasa Urdu sebelumnya.

future_work.en: The authors note that cross-lingual zero-shot evaluation alone does not establish full language-neutrality, pointing to the need for further investigation into language-neutral representations and robustness.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa evaluasi *cross-lingual zero-shot* saja belum menetapkan kenetralan bahasa yang penuh, yang menunjukkan perlunya investigasi lebih lanjut mengenai representasi yang netral terhadap bahasa dan ketahanannya.

method.en: The proposed multimodal multitask model integrates acoustic representations from wav2vec 2.0 and textual representations from XLM-R using cross-modal attention. Joint valence-arousal learning is incorporated alongside emotion classification, and the approach is evaluated using the Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus with rigorous testing protocols including speaker-independent splits and cross-lingual zero-shot transfer.
method.id: Model *multitask* multimodal yang diusulkan mengintegrasikan representasi akustik dari wav2vec 2.0 dan representasi tekstual dari XLM-R menggunakan *cross-modal attention*. Pembelajaran *valence-arousal* gabungan disertakan di samping klasifikasi emosi, dan pendekatan ini dievaluasi menggunakan korpus Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus dengan protokol pengujian yang ketat termasuk pemisahan *speaker-independent* dan transfer *cross-lingual zero-shot*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan terkait secara mendetail.

results.en: The proposed model achieves 91.3 percent emotion recognition accuracy on the Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus, outperforming strong audio-only and text-only baselines. Joint valence-arousal learning consistently improves performance over emotion-only training, while cross-lingual zero-shot evaluation on English datasets yields 80.2 plus or minus 1.3 percent on IEMOCAP to 86.3 plus or minus 0.9 percent on CREMA-D without fine-tuning.
results.id: Model yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi pengenalan emosi sebesar 91,3 persen pada korpus Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus, mengungguli *baseline* yang hanya berbasis audio atau teks. Pembelajaran *valence-arousal* gabungan secara konsisten meningkatkan kinerja dibandingkan pelatihan khusus emosi, sementara evaluasi *cross-lingual zero-shot* pada *dataset* bahasa Inggris menghasilkan 80,2 plus minus 1,3 persen pada IEMOCAP hingga 86,3 plus minus 0,9 persen pada CREMA-D tanpa *fine-tuning*.

tldr.en: This paper introduces a cross-modal audio-text attention framework for speech emotion recognition in low-resource Urdu. The proposed model achieves 91.3 percent accuracy on the Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus and demonstrates strong cross-lingual zero-shot generalization.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan kerangka *cross-modal audio-text attention* untuk *speech emotion recognition* pada bahasa Urdu yang berstatus *low-resource*. Model yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi 91,3 persen pada korpus Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus serta menunjukkan generalisasi *zero-shot* lintas bahasa yang kuat.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69201-2.title: Cross-modal audio-text attention for multimodal multitask speech emotion recognition in low-resource Urdu

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69546-8.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) play a critical role in how humans access information. While their core functionality relies on the ability to comprehend written requests, our understanding of this ability is currently constrained, because most benchmarks evaluate LLMs in high-resource languages that are predominantly spoken by Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) communities. The default assumption is that English is the best-performing language for LLMs, while smaller, low-resource languages are linked to less natural or reliable outputs, even in multilingual, state-of-the-art models. To track fluctuations in the comprehension abilities of LLMs, we prompt 3 popular models across 12 languages, representing the Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Turkic, Sino-Tibetan, and Japonic language families. Our results suggest that the models exhibit remarkable accuracy across typologically diverse languages, yet they may fall behind human baselines, albeit to different degrees. Contrary to what was expected, English is not the best-performing language, as it was systematically outperformed by several Romance languages, even lower-resource ones. We frame the results by highlighting the role of factors that drive LLM performance, such as tokenization, language distance from Spanish and English, size of training data, and data origin in high- vs. low-resource languages and WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD communities.

Proses memecah teks menjadi unit-unit kecil yang disebut token agar dapat diproses oleh *large language model*.
Titik acuan atau kinerja awal yang digunakan untuk membandingkan hasil dari model yang diusulkan.

background.en: Large language models play a critical role in how humans access information, relying fundamentally on their ability to comprehend written requests. However, current understanding of this comprehension ability is constrained because most evaluation benchmarks focus on high-resource languages spoken predominantly by Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic communities. The prevailing assumption is that English serves as the best-performing language for these models, while low-resource languages typically yield less natural or reliable outputs, even in state-of-the-art multilingual systems. This creates a significant gap in our knowledge regarding how models handle linguistic diversity beyond dominant Western languages.
background.id: *Large language model* memainkan peran krusial dalam cara manusia mengakses informasi, yang secara fundamental bergantung pada kemampuan mereka untuk memahami permintaan tertulis. Namun, pemahaman saat ini mengenai kemampuan pemahaman ini terbatas karena sebagian besar *benchmark* evaluasi berfokus pada bahasa *high-resource* yang dituturkan secara dominan oleh komunitas *Western*, *Educated*, *Industrialized*, *Rich*, and *Democratic*. Asumsi yang berlaku adalah bahwa bahasa Inggris berfungsi sebagai bahasa dengan kinerja terbaik untuk model-model ini, sementara bahasa *low-resource* biasanya menghasilkan keluaran yang kurang alami atau andal, bahkan dalam sistem multibahasa *state-of-the-art*. Hal ini menciptakan kesenjangan yang signifikan dalam pengetahuan kita mengenai bagaimana model menangani keragaman linguistik di luar bahasa barat yang dominan.

contributions.en: The paper investigates the comprehension abilities of three popular large language models across twelve languages representing diverse language families, including Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Turkic, Sino-Tibetan, and Japonic. A key contribution is the empirical demonstration that model accuracy varies significantly across typologically diverse languages and that English does not consistently achieve the highest performance.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyelidiki kemampuan pemahaman dari tiga *large language model* populer di dua belas bahasa yang mewakili rumpun bahasa yang beragam, termasuk Indo-Eropa, Afro-Asiatik, Turkik, Sino-Tibet, dan Japonik. Kontribusi utamanya adalah demonstrasi empiris bahwa akurasi model bervariasi secara signifikan di berbagai bahasa yang secara tipologis beragam dan bahwa bahasa Inggris tidak secara konsisten mencapai kinerja tertinggi.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas *future work* secara mendetail.

method.en: The authors prompt three popular large language models across twelve languages from the Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Turkic, Sino-Tibetan, and Japonic language families. The evaluation framework tracks fluctuations in comprehension abilities across these diverse idioms to assess performance against human baselines. Furthermore, the analysis frames the results by examining several driving factors, including tokenization efficiency, language distance from Spanish and English, training data size, and the origin of data from high- versus low-resource languages and WEIRD versus non-WEIRD communities.
method.id: Para penulis meminta tanggapan dari tiga *large language model* populer di dua belas bahasa dari rumpun bahasa Indo-Eropa, Afro-Asiatik, Turkik, Sino-Tibet, dan Japonik. Kerangka evaluasi melacak fluktuasi kemampuan pemahaman di antara berbagai idiom yang beragam ini untuk menilai kinerja terhadap *baseline* manusia. Selain itu, analisis membingkai hasil dengan memeriksa beberapa faktor pendorong, termasuk efisiensi *tokenization*, jarak bahasa dari bahasa Spanyol dan Inggris, ukuran *training data*, dan asal data dari bahasa *high-resource* versus *low-resource* serta komunitas *WEIRD* versus non-*WEIRD*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas *related work* secara mendetail.

results.en: The results indicate that the models exhibit remarkable accuracy across typologically diverse languages, although they still fall behind human baselines to varying degrees. Contrary to standard expectations, English is systematically outperformed by several Romance languages, including lower-resource variants. The authors interpret these findings by highlighting key factors that drive performance, such as tokenization strategies, language distance to Spanish and English, training data volume, and data origin.
results.id: Hasil menunjukkan bahwa model menampilkan akurasi yang luar biasa di berbagai bahasa yang secara tipologis beragam, meskipun mereka masih tertinggal dari *baseline* manusia pada derajat yang berbeda-beda. Berlawanan dengan ekspektasi standar, bahasa Inggris secara sistematis dikalahkan oleh beberapa bahasa Roman, termasuk varian *lower-resource*. Para penulis menginterpretasikan temuan ini dengan menyoroti faktor-faktor kunci yang mendorong kinerja, seperti strategi *tokenization*, jarak bahasa ke bahasa Spanyol dan Inggris, volume *training data*, dan asal data.

tldr.en: This paper evaluates the reading comprehension capabilities of three popular large language models across twelve typologically diverse languages. The findings reveal that models do not perform equally across languages, with several Romance languages unexpectedly outperforming English.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengevaluasi kemampuan pemahaman membaca dari tiga *large language model* populer di dua belas bahasa yang secara tipologis beragam. Temuannya mengungkapkan bahwa model tidak berkinerja secara merata di berbagai bahasa, dengan beberapa bahasa Roman secara tak terduga mengungguli bahasa Inggris.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69546-8.title: Multilingual large language models do not comprehend all natural languages to equal degrees

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70314-x.abstract: A noise-robust framework is introduced for semi-supervised cross-lingual financial ontology induction, designed to address the challenges posed by noisy and partially labeled multilingual financial documents. The method employs a confidence-based filtering mechanism to eliminate low-quality cross-lingual text pairs, followed by multi-view distillation to harmonize linguistic and structural representations of financial entities. An uncertainty-aware contrastive learning objective further aligns entities across languages while reducing the influence of unreliable alignments. The resulting ontology is incorporated into an adaptive multilingual NER pipeline using entity-aware attention, enabling the model to exploit cross-lingual consistency for enhanced recognition performance. The overall approach integrates these components to construct a robust financial ontology using minimal labeled data while maintaining interpretability through high-confidence alignments. Experiments on multilingual financial corpora demonstrate strong effectiveness in noisy conditions, surpassing existing methods in both ontology quality and downstream NER tasks. The framework's capacity to adapt to low-resource languages and manage label noise makes it well suited for real-world financial environments characterized by scarce and heterogeneous annotated data.

glossary.explanation_id: Financial ontology adalah representasi terstruktur dari pengetahuan keuangan yang mendefinisikan konsep dan hubungan antar-entitas dalam domain keuangan.
Semi-supervised adalah pendekatan pelatihan *model bahasa* yang menggunakan kombinasi data beranotasi dan data tak beranotasi.
Multi-view distillation adalah teknik transfer pengetahuan yang menyelaraskan berbagai representasi dari sudut pandang yang berbeda.
Contrastive learning adalah metode *machine learning* untuk mendekatkan representasi data yang serupa dan menjauhkan data yang berbeda.
NER pipeline adalah rangkaian tahapan pemrosesan untuk tugas *Named Entity Recognition* guna mengekstrak entitas bernama dari teks.
Entity-aware attention adalah mekanisme perhatian dalam *neural network* yang secara khusus memperhitungkan informasi entitas.

background.en: Real-world financial environments are often characterized by scarce and heterogeneous annotated data, alongside noisy and partially labeled multilingual financial documents. Addressing these challenges is critical for effective document recognition, yet existing approaches struggle with label noise and low-resource constraints.
background.id: Lingkungan keuangan dunia nyata sering kali ditandai dengan sedikitnya data beranotasi dan heterogen, serta dokumen keuangan multilingual yang berderau dan berlabel sebagian. Mengatasi tantangan ini sangat penting untuk pengenalan dokumen yang efektif, namun pendekatan yang ada masih kesulitan menghadapi derau label dan kendala *low-resource*.

contributions.en: The paper introduces a noise-robust framework for semi-supervised cross-lingual financial ontology induction. The main contributions include a confidence-based filtering mechanism, multi-view distillation, an uncertainty-aware contrastive learning objective, and an adaptive multilingual NER pipeline using entity-aware attention.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *framework* yang tahan terhadap derau untuk induksi *financial ontology* lintas bahasa secara semi-supervisi. Kontribusi utamanya mencakup mekanisme penyaringan berbasis *confidence*, *multi-view distillation*, fungsi *contrastive learning* yang *uncertainty-aware*, serta *pipeline* *NER* multilingual adaptif yang menggunakan *entity-aware attention*.

future_work.en: The paper does not state future work explicitly.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak menyatakan pekerjaan masa depan secara eksplisit.

method.en: The method employs a confidence-based filtering mechanism to eliminate low-quality cross-lingual text pairs, followed by multi-view distillation to harmonize linguistic and structural representations. It applies an uncertainty-aware contrastive learning objective to align entities across languages while reducing the influence of unreliable alignments, and incorporates the resulting ontology into an adaptive multilingual NER pipeline using entity-aware attention.
method.id: Metode ini menggunakan mekanisme penyaringan berbasis *confidence* untuk mengeliminasi pasang teks lintas bahasa berkualitas rendah, diikuti oleh *multi-view distillation* untuk mengharmonisasi representasi linguistik dan struktural. Metode ini menerapkan fungsi *contrastive learning* yang *uncertainty-aware* untuk menyelaraskan entitas antarbahasa sekaligus mengurangi pengaruh penyelarasan yang tidak andal, serta memasukkan *ontology* yang dihasilkan ke dalam *pipeline* *NER* multilingual adaptif menggunakan *entity-aware attention*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas karya terkait secara rinci.

results.en: Experiments on multilingual financial corpora demonstrate strong effectiveness in noisy conditions, surpassing existing methods in both ontology quality and downstream NER tasks. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that the framework successfully adapts to low-resource languages and manages label noise.
results.id: Eksperimen pada korpus keuangan multilingual menunjukkan efektivitas yang kuat dalam kondisi berderau, melampaui metode yang ada baik dalam kualitas *ontology* maupun tugas *NER* hilir. Para penulis menafsirkan temuan ini sebagai bukti bahwa *framework* tersebut berhasil beradaptasi dengan bahasa *low-resource* dan mengelola derau label.

tldr.en: This paper introduces a noise-robust framework for semi-supervised cross-lingual financial ontology induction using multilingual financial documents. Experiments demonstrate strong effectiveness in noisy conditions, surpassing existing methods in ontology quality and downstream NER tasks.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *framework* yang tahan terhadap derau untuk induksi *financial ontology* lintas bahasa secara semi-supervisi menggunakan dokumen keuangan multilingual. Eksperimen menunjukkan efektivitas yang kuat dalam kondisi berderau, melampaui metode yang ada dalam kualitas *ontology* dan tugas *NER* hilir.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-71065-5.abstract: Edge translation systems must balance limited computation, data locality, and weak performance on low-resource language pairs. This study presents Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning (MT-BayesFL), a multilingual translation framework that combines a lightweight shared encoder, task-specific decoders, matrix-normal posteriors over shared attention projections, and covariance-aware server aggregation. Client-side variational inference estimates posterior statistics that are fused by positive-semidefinite mixture moment matching, while Top-K transmission and KL regularization support communication-efficient training under non-IID data. An optional client-level differential-privacy release is defined only for a trusted or secure aggregation boundary and is reported as conditional privacy accounting rather than as part of the individual-update reconstruction diagnostic. Across five English-to-X tasks, MT-BayesFL is not uniformly strongest on high-resource pairs, where AdapterFL yields higher BLEU for English-Chinese, English-French, and English-German. Its largest descriptive advantages occur on English-Russian and English-Swahili, with BLEU scores of 32.6 and 28.3, respectively, together with an ECE of 0.082 on English-Swahili, 92.1% performance retention at 30% device dropout, a 1.786 MB upload per participating client per round, and lower reconstruction fidelity in the disclosed single-sentence no-DP diagnostic (TRA = 0.12; CosSim = 0.31). Under the separately specified aggregate release, the verified privacy accountant gives epsilon = 12.53 at delta = 0.00001; no end-to-end privacy-utility claim is made for that optional path.

glossary.explanation_id: Pembelajaran terdesentralisasi di mana model dilatih di beberapa perangkat yang memegang *data* lokal tanpa bertukar *data* mentah.
Metode aproksimasi statistik untuk menyelesaikan masalah inferensi intrakabel dalam *model* probabilitas.
Kerangka kerja matematis untuk memastikan bahwa keberadaan atau ketiadaan satu sampel individu tidak memengaruhi hasil keluaran *model* secara signifikan.
*Data* yang tidak terdistribusi secara identik dan independen di antara klien yang berbeda dalam jaringan.
*Metrik* standar untuk *evaluasi* kualitas *terjemahan mesin* dengan membandingkan teks hasil keluaran dengan referensi manusia.
*Metrik* yang mengukur kalibrasi probabilitas prediksi dari sebuah *model* klasifikasi atau *neural network*.

background.en: Edge translation systems must balance limited computation, data locality, and weak performance on low-resource language pairs. Addressing these challenges is difficult because decentralized clients often hold non-IID data while operating under strict communication constraints and resource limitations.
background.id: Sistem terjemahan *edge* harus menyeimbangkan komputasi yang terbatas, lokalitas data, serta performa yang lemah pada pasangan bahasa *low-resource*. Mengatasi tantangan ini sulit karena klien terdesentralisasi sering kali memegang data non-IID saat beroperasi di bawah batasan komunikasi dan keterbatasan sumber daya yang ketat.

contributions.en: The study presents Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning (MT-BayesFL), a multilingual translation framework combining a lightweight shared encoder, task-specific decoders, matrix-normal posteriors over shared attention projections, and covariance-aware server aggregation. Additional contributions include communication-efficient training via Top-K transmission and KL regularization, and an optional client-level differential-privacy release.
contributions.id: Studi ini menyajikan *Multitask Bayesian Federated Learning* (*MT-BayesFL*), sebuah kerangka *terjemahan mesin* multibagas yang menggabungkan *encoder* bersama yang ringan, *decoder* khusus tugas, posterior *matrix-normal* atas proyeksi *attention* bersama, dan agregasi server yang sadar kovarians. Kontribusi tambahan mencakup pelatihan yang efisien komunikasi melalui transmisi Top-K dan regularisasi KL, serta rilis *differential privacy* tingkat klien opsional.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan secara rinci.

method.en: Client-side variational inference estimates posterior statistics that are fused by positive-semidefinite mixture moment matching, while Top-K transmission and KL regularization support communication-efficient training under non-IID data. An optional client-level differential-privacy release is defined only for a trusted or secure aggregation boundary and is reported as conditional privacy accounting rather than as part of the individual-update reconstruction diagnostic.
method.id: *Variational inference* di sisi klien memperkirakan statistik posterior yang digabungkan oleh *positive-semidefinite mixture moment matching*, sementara transmisi Top-K dan regularisasi KL mendukung pelatihan yang efisien komunikasi di bawah data non-IID. Rilis *differential privacy* tingkat klien opsional didefinisikan hanya untuk batas agregasi yang tepercaya atau aman dan dilaporkan sebagai akuntansi privasi bersondisional alih-alih sebagai bagian dari diagnostik rekonstruksi pembaruan individual.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan terkait secara rinci.

results.en: Across five English-to-X tasks, MT-BayesFL is not uniformly strongest on high-resource pairs, where AdapterFL yields higher BLEU for English-Chinese, English-French, and English-German. Its largest descriptive advantages occur on English-Russian and English-Swahili, with BLEU scores of 32.6 and 28.3, respectively, together with an ECE of 0.082 on English-Swahili, 92.1% performance retention at 30% device dropout, a 1.786 MB upload per participating client per round, and lower reconstruction fidelity in the disclosed single-sentence no-DP diagnostic (TRA = 0.12; CosSim = 0.31). Under the separately specified aggregate release, the verified privacy accountant gives epsilon = 12.53 at delta = 0.00001; no end-to-end privacy-utility claim is made for that optional path.
results.id: Lintas lima tugas English-to-X, *MT-BayesFL* tidak secara seragam terkuat pada pasangan *high-resource*, di mana *AdapterFL* menghasilkan BLEU yang lebih tinggi untuk English-Chinese, English-French, and English-German. Keunggulan deskriptif terbesarnya terjadi pada English-Russian dan English-Swahili, dengan skor BLEU masing-masing 32.6 dan 28.3, beserta ECE sebesar 0.082 pada English-Swahili, retensi performa 92.1% pada *device dropout* 30%, unggahan 1.786 MB per klien yang berpartisipasi per putaran, dan fidelitas rekonstruksi yang lebih rendah pada diagnostik tanpa-DP satu kalimat yang diungkapkan (TRA = 0.12; CosSim = 0.31). Di bawah rilis agregat yang ditentukan secara terpisah, akuntan privasi yang diverifikasi memberikan epsilon = 12.53 pada delta = 0.00001; tidak ada klaim privasi-utilitas *end-to-end* yang dibuat untuk jalur opsional tersebut.

tldr.en: This paper introduces MT-BayesFL, a multitask Bayesian federated learning framework designed for multilingual translation at the edge. The method achieves robust translation performance on low-resource language pairs while maintaining communication efficiency and uncertainty awareness.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *MT-BayesFL*, sebuah kerangka *federated learning* Bayesian multibagas untuk *terjemahan mesin* di *edge*. Metode ini mencapai performa terjemahan yang kuat pada pasangan bahasa *low-resource* sambil mempertahankan efisiensi komunikasi dan kesadaran ketidakpastian.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-71065-5.title: Uncertainty-aware Bayesian federated learning for low-resource neural machine translation at the edge

doi:10.1080/1369118x.2026.2713663.abstract: Given the dynamic and constantly evolving character of domestic online influence operations (IO), more knowledge of how these operations are changing is critical for efforts to counter the corrosive effects of IO on democracy and public debate. This article analyses the evolution of IO in Thailand, Indonesia, and the Philippines, using interviews with individuals involved in executing such operations. We identify a five-fold transformation. First, we trace a shift from state-dominated influence campaigns to a broader spectrum of clients. Second, we observe increased outsourcing of the operational work to private companies and freelancers. Third, we find a shift from quantity to quality in social media accounts, with IO workers operating fewer, more carefully crafted and influential profiles, alongside more limited use of automated bots. Fourth, content strategies have matured: instead of simply echoing state narratives, contemporary IO use data analytics to craft content tailored to specific audiences, often through subtle reframing of news rather than blatant disinformation. Fifth, dissemination methods have similarly shifted – from overwhelming social platforms with content to a more responsive, targeted, and data-informed approach. These changes signal a move toward more refined and strategic influence tactics. We conclude by highlighting likely causes of these transformations, and discuss implications for efforts to counter IO.
doi:10.1080/1369118x.2026.2713663.title: Influence operations 2.0: the evolution of social media manipulation in Southeast Asia

doi:10.1080/23322039.2026.2728275.abstract: Foreign direct investment (FDI) is an unavoidable factor in the global economy that determines economic development, including gender equality. Indonesia is one of the developing countries attracting significant investment in Southeast Asia. However, data on gender inequality shows a relatively high figure and has experienced a slow decline over the past five years (from 0.488 in 2019 to 0.447 in 2023). Considering this, the objective of this study is to investigate the effect of FDI on gender inequality in Indonesia by utilizing micro-survey data at the firm level from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys (WBES). Using a linear regression model, our findings indicate that FDI negatively affects gender inequality, suggesting that higher FDI tends to widen it. Our findings also confirm robustness across various model scenarios, including the PSM-DID and panel logit regression model.

Model regresi logistik yang dirancang khusus untuk menganalisis data panel dengan variabel dependen biner.

background.en: Foreign direct investment is an unavoidable factor in the global economy that determines economic development, including gender equality. Indonesia is one of the developing countries attracting significant investment in Southeast Asia. However, data on gender inequality shows a relatively high figure and has experienced a slow decline over the past five years, moving from 0.488 in 2019 to 0.447 in 2023. Given this situation, the study investigates the specific effect of foreign direct investment on gender inequality in the country.

Indonesia adalah salah satu negara berkembang yang menarik investasi signifikan di Asia Tenggara. Mempertimbangkan situasi ini, penelitian ini menyelidiki efek spesifik dari *foreign direct investment* terhadap ketimpangan gender di negara tersebut.

contributions.en: The study contributes by investigating the direct effect of foreign direct investment on gender inequality in Indonesian firms. By utilizing micro-survey data at the firm level, the research provides empirical evidence on how external investment interacts with social disparities in a major developing economy.

It employs a linear regression model to estimate the relationship between foreign direct investment and gender inequality. Furthermore, the authors confirm robustness across various model scenarios, including the propensity score matching difference-in-differences and panel logit regression models.

Additionally, the findings confirm robustness across various model scenarios, including the propensity score matching difference-in-differences and panel logit regression model, reinforcing the reliability of the negative impact.
results.id: Temuan empiris menunjukkan bahwa *foreign direct investment* berdampak negatif terhadap ketimpangan gender, menyiratkan bahwa *foreign direct investment* yang lebih tinggi cenderung memperlebar ketimpangan di dalam perusahaan. Selain itu, temuan mengonfirmasi ketahanan di berbagai skenario model, termasuk model *PSM-DID* dan *panel logit regression*, yang memperkuat keandalan dampak negatif tersebut.

tldr.en: This paper investigates the effect of foreign direct investment on gender inequality in Indonesian firms using firm-level micro-survey data. The findings indicate that higher foreign direct investment negatively affects gender inequality by tending to widen it.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti efek *foreign direct investment* terhadap ketimpangan gender di perusahaan-perusahaan Indonesia menggunakan data mikro tingkat perusahaan. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa *foreign direct investment* yang lebih tinggi berdampak negatif pada ketimpangan gender dengan kecenderungan memperlebarnya.

doi:10.1093/gji/ggag341.abstract: SUMMARY The statistics of earthquake populations are governed by stress changes and event interactions at various scales which promote nonlinear event cascades and seismicity clustering. Earthquake clustering in space and time is observed in both tectonic and volcanically dominated regions; however, notable differences exist for instance during eruptive sequences. Here, we characterize seismicity statistics in California and Hawaii and quantify differences in background rates and clustering. We compare three statistical approaches, that is, (i) Reasenberg declustering, (ii) Gamma distribution fit and (iii) Nearest Neighbour Clustering which are applied to seismicity in Hawaii, southern California and Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) catalogues with known clustering characteristics. Tests with ETAS-catalogues suggest that background rate variations are more consistently resolvable using the Nearest Neighbour and Gamma distribution algorithm without requiring parameter adjustments to the specific study area. The Nearest Neighbour method tends to overestimate background rates, whereas the Gamma distribution algorithm shows systematic underestimation, suggesting that an ensemble model can improve the performance over any single method. Uncertainties in background rate estimates based on small magnitude events (e.g. M $\ge$ 2.5) are high, in particular for the Reasenberg method, which overpredicts true rates by up to a factor of 4, and extrapolations to larger magnitudes need to be treated cautiously. Our analysis shows that the combination of the three approaches generates new insights into the processes that govern seismicity clustering. The analysis of southern California seismicity produces consistent results between the different methods, and the distribution of background seismicity rates is indistinguishable from Poissonian rates at magnitudes above 3.5. Conversely, the seismicity in Hawaii exhibits notable non-Poissonian background rate changes. Results from the Nearest Neighbour clustering analysis suggest notable differences between tectonic and volcano seismicity, including background rate changes and more pronounced spatiotemporal clustering around active volcanoes. Hawaiian seismicity is characterized by more localized spatial-temporal clustering, in particular during the 2018 eruption. This difference may be a result of magmatic, hydrothermal and eruptive processes, which make volcanic areas susceptible to stress perturbations and earthquake triggering at small scales.
doi:10.1093/gji/ggag341.title: Characterizing differences in seismicity clustering and background rates between Hawaii and California

doi:10.1108/par-11-2025-0285.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how Fijian firms navigate the intersection of global environment, social and governance (ESG) mandates and local institutional constraints. It investigates technology adoption as a symbolic resource rather than a neutral enabler of transparency in small island developing states (SIDS). Design/methodology/approach Adopting an interpretive research paradigm and a managerial sensemaking lens, this research utilises a qualitative multi-case study design. Data was gathered through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with senior executives from firms listed on the South Pacific Stock Exchange (SPX) and a critical review of corporate disclosures. Findings The results reveal a front-stage and back-stage dichotomy where firms utilise digital infrastructures as a technological veil. In Fiji’s low-enforcement environment, imported coercive pressures from global bodies like the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) drive a legitimacy-first pathway. This leads to digital decoupling, where impressive digital outputs mask manual and resource-constrained operational realities. Furthermore, the study distinguishes between deceptive greenwashing and pragmatic scaling, a sensemaking strategy used to bridge the gap between global expectations and local expertise gaps. Originality/value This research extends institutional theory to examine the digital-substantive gap in emerging economies. By introducing digital decoupling, it offers a framework for understanding how technology facilitates symbolic compliance in SIDS, providing insights for regulators at the Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) and SPX to move beyond digital facades towards substantive accountability.
doi:10.1108/par-11-2025-0285.title: Technology adoption and institutional influences on ESG reporting: an interpretive study of South Pacific Stock Exchange (SPX) listed companies

doi:10.1111/exsy.70431.abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐source large language models (LLMs) have significantly advanced natural language processing (NLP), particularly for English. However, their performance in Arabic has remained limited due to the scarcity of high‐quality datasets and the high computational cost of full fine‐tuning. To address this challenge, we curated and prepared a diverse collection of Arabic‐specific datasets covering translation, summarization, storytelling, dialogue generation, and Classical–Modern Arabic bridging. Building on these resources, we developed ArGemma, an Arabic‐adapted version of the Gemma model, fine‐tuned using Supervised Fine‐Tuning (SFT) with Low‐Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to enable efficient adaptation with reduced computational overhead. A hybrid approach integrating SFT, Retrieval‐Augmented Generation (RAG), and few‐shot prompting was also employed to enhance contextual understanding and performance—particularly for tasks requiring nuanced reasoning across different forms of Arabic. ArGemma's performance was evaluated using both quantitative metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) and qualitative assessments by native speakers and language experts to measure fluency, coherence, and contextual accuracy. Results demonstrate that LoRA‐based fine‐tuning, supported by carefully prepared datasets and retrieval‐augmented techniques, can significantly enhance Arabic NLP performance while remaining computationally efficient. This work, which was awarded third place in the 2025 Google—Unlock Global Communication with Gemma Kaggle competition, demonstrates how parameter‐efficient fine‐tuning (PEFT) combined with targeted dataset preparation can effectively expand LLM support for underrepresented languages like Arabic.

glossary.explanation_id: *Low-Rank Adaptation* adalah teknik *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang melatih matriks rank rendah untuk mengurangi jumlah parameter yang dapat dilatih.
*Supervised Fine-Tuning* adalah proses pelatihan lanjutan pada *large language model* menggunakan data beranotasi untuk tugas tertentu.
*Retrieval-Augmented Generation* adalah pendekatan yang menggabungkan pencarian dokumen eksternal dengan pembangkitan teks oleh *large language model*.
*Few-shot prompting* adalah metode pemberian beberapa contoh masukan dan keluaran dalam *prompt* untuk membimbing *large language model*.
*Parameter-efficient fine-tuning* adalah metode penyesuaian *large language model* yang hanya melatih sebagian kecil parameter dari model keseluruhan.

background.en: Open-source large language models have significantly advanced natural language processing, particularly for English. However, their performance in Arabic has remained limited due to the scarcity of high-quality datasets and the high computational cost of full fine-tuning.

They developed ArGemma by fine-tuning the Gemma model using Supervised Fine-Tuning with Low-Rank Adaptation to enable efficient adaptation with reduced computational overhead. Additionally, a hybrid approach integrating Supervised Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and few-shot prompting was employed to enhance contextual understanding. results.id: Hasil menunjukkan bahwa penyempurnaan berbasis *Low-Rank Adaptation*, yang didukung oleh kumpulan data yang disiapkan secara cermat dan teknik *retrieval-augmented*, dapat secara signifikan meningkatkan kinerja *natural language processing* bahasa Arab sambil tetap efisien secara komputasi. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan yang efisien parameter ini secara signifikan meningkatkan kinerja *natural language processing* dalam bahasa Arab dengan beban komputasi yang lebih rendah.

doi:10.11113/humentech.v5n2.144.abstract: As global tourism continues to expand, effective communication between tourists and local communities remains a persistent challenge. This paper presents the development and evaluation of My Loghat!, an interactive mobile e-learning application designed to teach Malay language dialects from four Malaysian states — Terengganu, Kedah, Sabah, and Perak — to tourists. Guided by the Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) methodology, the application integrated audio recordings of native dialect speakers, visual aids, culturally contextualised content (state history, traditional costumes, and notable places), and gamified quizzes. The system was implemented using Adobe Animate, Audacity, and Canva, and deployed as an Android APK. A structured evaluation was conducted involving two multimedia experts and 20 target users, assessed across three dimensions: content quality, effectiveness, and user satisfaction, using a four-point Likert scale. The results demonstrated strong overall acceptance, with 54.1% of target user responded at the 'Agree' level and 45.9% at 'Strongly Agree'. All responses were positive, indicating no disagreement with the application's features. The expert evaluations similarly yielded predominantly positive assessments. The findings suggest that My Loghat! represents a viable, accessible, and engaging tool for improving dialect comprehension and cultural immersion among tourists visiting Malaysia. The study contributes to the growing body of literature on mobile-assisted language learning (MALL) and cultural heritage preservation through technology.
authors: Che Ku Nuraini Che Ku Mohd
doi:10.11113/humentech.v5n2.144.title: My Loghat!: Design, Development, and Evaluation of a Mobile Multimedia Application for Malay Dialect Learning and Cultural Immersion in Tourism

doi:10.1142/s0218001426400562.abstract: Cross-lingual semantic alignment and data scarcity remain two major challenges for low-resource language pairs in neural machine translation (NMT), particularly when developing translation models with crossdomain adaptability. This study proposes a Chinese–Japanese NMT framework that integrates the pre-trained cross-lingual model Cross-lingual Language Model–RoBERTa (XLM-R) with a Dynamic Weighted Iterative Back-Translation for Data Augmentation (DWIB-DA) strategy. The key innovation lies in enhancing crosslingual semantic representations through multilingual shared vocabularies and large-scale pretraining, while constructing high-quality pseudo-parallel corpora through dynamic weight adjustment and adversarial training mechanisms. Specifically, XLM-R achieves bilingual semantic space alignment by leveraging multilingual masked language modeling and shared lexical representations. The proposed DWIB-DA strategy dynamically calculates domain relevance and semantic similarity weights to select and generate high-quality pseudo-parallel data. Furthermore, adversarial training is incorporated to enhance the domain adaptability and robustness of the augmented corpus. By combining cross-lingual pretraining with dynamic data augmentation, the proposed framework effectively addresses the challenges of limited training resources and domain variation in Chinese–Japanese NMT. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a BLEU score of 38.9 on general-domain test sets, outperforming the baseline XLM-Transformer by 3.3 points. Under low-resource conditions with only 20% of the original training data, the model maintains a BLEU score of 31.2, indicating strong translation capability with limited supervision. In a domain-specific popular science translation task, the proposed model improves the BLEU score by 4.1 points to 33.0, demonstrating enhanced domain adaptability in specialized translation scenarios. Human evaluation further confirms the superiority of the proposed model in terms of fluency (4.3), semantic accuracy (4.2), and terminological consistency (4.0) compared with the baseline model. These findings provide theoretical insights into the synergistic effects of cross-lingual pretraining and dynamic data augmentation, while offering practical technical references for the development of translation systems targeting similar low-resource language pairs.
doi:10.1142/s0218001426400562.journal_ref: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence

glossary.explanation_id: Neural machine translation adalah pendekatan *terjemahan mesin* yang menggunakan jaringan saraf tiruan untuk memetakan seluruh kalimat sumber ke kalimat sasaran.
Kondisi low-resource merujuk pada situasi di mana ketersediaan data pelatihan atau sumber daya komputasi untuk suatu bahasa sangat terbatas.
Data augmentation adalah teknik untuk memperbesar ukuran dan keragaman *korpus* pelatihan dengan menghasilkan data sintetis tambahan.
Pseudo-parallel corpora adalah kumpulan data terjemahan buatan yang dihasilkan secara otomatis menggunakan model komputer daripada dibuat langsung oleh penerjemah manusia.
Adversarial training adalah teknik pelatihan *model bahasa* di mana model dilatih menggunakan contoh sulit atau manipulasi data untuk meningkatkan ketahanan.
BLEU score adalah *metrik* evaluasi standar yang digunakan untuk mengukur kualitas teks *terjemahan mesin* dibandingkan dengan referensi manusia.
Baseline adalah model standar atau sistem pembanding yang digunakan untuk mengukur peningkatan performa dari model baru yang diusulkan.

background.en: Cross-lingual semantic alignment and data scarcity remain two major challenges for low-resource language pairs in neural machine translation, particularly when developing translation models with cross-domain adaptability.
background.id: Penyelarasan semantik lintas bahasa dan kelangkaan data tetap menjadi dua tantangan utama untuk pasangan bahasa *low-resource* dalam *neural machine translation*, khususnya ketika mengembangkan model terjemahan dengan kemampuan adaptasi lintas domain.

contributions.en: This study proposes a Chinese-Japanese neural machine translation framework that integrates the pre-trained cross-lingual model Cross-lingual Language Model-RoBERTa with a Dynamic Weighted Iterative Back-Translation for Data Augmentation strategy. The key innovation lies in enhancing cross-lingual semantic representations through multilingual shared vocabularies and large-scale pretraining, while constructing high-quality pseudo-parallel corpora through dynamic weight adjustment and adversarial training mechanisms.
contributions.id: Studi ini mengusulkan kerangka *neural machine translation* bahasa Mandarin-Jepang yang mengintegrasikan model lintas bahasa *pre-trained* *Cross-lingual Language Model-RoBERTa* dengan strategi *Dynamic Weighted Iterative Back-Translation for Data Augmentation*. Inovasi utamanya terletak pada peningkatan representasi semantik lintas bahasa melalui *vocabulary* bersama multilingual dan *pre-training* berskala besar, sekaligus membangun *korpus* pseudo-paralel berkualitas tinggi melalui penyesuaian bobot dinamis dan mekanisme *adversarial training*.

method.en: Cross-lingual Language Model-RoBERTa achieves bilingual semantic space alignment by leveraging multilingual masked language modeling and shared lexical representations. The proposed Dynamic Weighted Iterative Back-Translation for Data Augmentation strategy dynamically calculates domain relevance and semantic similarity weights to select and generate high-quality pseudo-parallel data, while adversarial training is incorporated to enhance domain adaptability and robustness.

results.en: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a BLEU score of 38.9 on general-domain test sets, outperforming the baseline XLM-Transformer by 3.3 points. doi:10.1145/3832259.abstract: COBOL remains critical across banking, insurance, and government infrastructure. However, maintenance is increasingly challenging due to outdated technologies, sparse documentation, and developer retirement, necessitating code translation into modern languages like C. Traditional rule-based transcompilers yield outputs that are difficult to read and maintain, while general-purpose large language models (LLMs) achieve suboptimal correctness because COBOL is a low-resource language with distinct logic patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose SEDCoT, a novel COBOL-to-C translation framework. SEDCoT first leverages LLMs for initial translation, then combines symbolic execution with LLM guidance to generate test suites and iteratively repair semantic discrepancies. Finally, it integrates delta debugging to minimize failing tests into succinct counterexamples, accelerating automated code repair. Evaluating SEDCoT on a public COBOL-to-C dataset demonstrates that it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by at least 12% while producing translations with substantially higher readability than rule-based alternatives.
doi:10.1145/3832259.journal_ref: Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.

glossary.explanation_id: *Transcompiler* adalah alat yang menerjemahkan kode sumber dari satu bahasa pemrograman ke bahasa pemrograman lain dengan tingkat abstraksi yang serupa.
*Symbolic execution* adalah teknik analisis program yang menggunakan nilai simbolis alih-alih nilai konkret untuk menjelajahi berbagai jalur eksekusi.
*Delta debugging* adalah teknik otomatis untuk mengisolasi penyebab kegagalan dalam program dengan menyederhanakan masukan yang gagal.
*Test suite* adalah kumpulan kasus uji yang dirancang untuk menguji apakah suatu program berfungsi dengan benar.
*Counterexample* adalah contoh spesifik yang membuktikan bahwa suatu klaim atau properti program bernilai salah.

background.en: COBOL remains critical across banking, insurance, and government infrastructure. However, maintenance is increasingly challenging due to outdated technologies, sparse documentation, and developer retirement, necessitating code translation into modern languages like C. Traditional rule-based transcompilers yield outputs that are difficult to read and maintain, while general-purpose large language models achieve suboptimal correctness because COBOL is a low-resource language with distinct logic patterns.

doi:10.1145/3837066.abstract: Sequence labeling tasks such as part-of-speech (POS) tagging and named entity recognition (NER) have advanced significantly in high-resource languages and well-structured texts. However, low-resource languages, such as Urdu, face unique challenges due to limited annotated resources, complex morphology, and the informal, noisy nature of social media text. To address this, we introduce two relatively large-scale annotated datasets of Urdu tweets: a POS tagging dataset with 39 syntactic tags and an NER dataset covering three major entity types (person, location, and organization), capturing the linguistic diversity of user-generated content. We benchmark these datasets using a spectrum of approaches, from traditional conditional random fields (CRFs) to deep neural architectures with static embeddings and fine-tuned pre-trained language models (PLMs). Building on these findings, we propose a transformer-based hybrid architecture, XLM-R–CNN–BiLSTM–CRF, which integrates XLM-R embeddings for contextualized representation, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for local feature extraction, bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks for sequential modeling, and a CRF layer for optimal sequence prediction. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, with F1 scores of 95.39% for POS tagging and 91.91% for NER, significantly surpassing strong baselines. These resources and methods advance sequence labeling for Urdu while providing insights for other low-resource, noisy languages.

glossary.explanation_id: Pelabelan urutan adalah tugas menetapkan label kategori ke setiap token dalam urutan teks.
Penandaan *part-of-speech* adalah proses penentuan kelas kata seperti kata benda atau kata kerja pada setiap kata dalam kalimat.
Pengenalan entitas bernama adalah tugas mengidentifikasi dan mengklasifikasikan entitas seperti orang, lokasi, dan organisasi di dalam teks.
*Conditional random field* adalah jenis kerangka kerja pemodelan statistik yang sering digunakan untuk pemodelan terstruktur dan pelabelan urutan.
*Static embedding* adalah representasi vektor kata di mana setiap kata memiliki satu representasi tetap terlepas dari konteks kalimatnya.
*Fine-tuning* adalah proses penyesuaian lanjutan pada *pre-trained language model* menggunakan data spesifik untuk tugas tertentu.
Arsitektur hibrida adalah desain model yang menggabungkan dua atau lebih jenis jaringan saraf atau modul yang berbeda.

background.en: Sequence labeling tasks such as part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition have advanced significantly in high-resource languages and well-structured texts. However, low-resource languages like Urdu face unique challenges due to limited annotated resources, complex morphology, and the informal, noisy nature of social media text, creating a gap that this paper addresses.

Namun, bahasa *low-resource* seperti bahasa Urdu menghadapi tantangan unik karena keterbatasan sumber daya beranotasi, morfologi yang kompleks, serta sifat teks media sosial yang informal dan penuh derau, sehingga memunculkan kesenjangan yang diselesaikan dalam makalah ini.

contributions.en: The paper introduces two relatively large-scale annotated datasets of Urdu tweets: a part-of-speech tagging dataset with 39 syntactic tags and a named entity recognition dataset covering three major entity types. Furthermore, it proposes a novel transformer-based hybrid architecture, XLM-R–CNN–BiLSTM–CRF, which achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Selain itu, makalah ini mengusulkan arsitektur hibrida berbasis *transformer* yang baru, yaitu XLM-R–CNN–BiLSTM–CRF, yang mencapai performa *state-of-the-art*.

method.en: The study benchmarks the datasets using a spectrum of approaches ranging from traditional conditional random fields to deep neural architectures with static embeddings and fine-tuned pre-trained language models. The proposed XLM-R–CNN–BiLSTM–CRF architecture integrates XLM-R embeddings for contextualized representation, convolutional neural networks for local feature extraction, bidirectional long short-term memory networks for sequential modeling, and a conditional random field layer for optimal sequence prediction.

Arsitektur hibrida XLM-R–CNN–BiLSTM–CRF yang diusulkan mengintegrasikan *embedding* XLM-R untuk representasi terkontekstualisasi, *convolutional neural network* untuk ekstraksi fitur lokal, *bidirectional long short-term memory network* untuk pemodelan sekuensial, dan lapisan *conditional random field* untuk prediksi urutan yang optimal.

results.en: The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, with F1 scores of 95.39 percent for part-of-speech tagging and 91.91 percent for named entity recognition, significantly surpassing strong baselines. The authors interpret these results as an advancement for sequence labeling in Urdu and a provider of insights for other low-resource, noisy languages.

tldr.en: This paper introduces two annotated datasets of Urdu tweets for sequence labeling and proposes a transformer-based hybrid architecture. The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance for part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition on social media texts.

Model yang diusulkan mencapai performa *state-of-the-art* untuk penandaan kelas kata dan pengenalan entitas bernama pada teks media sosial.

doi:10.1145/3837853.abstract: This article investigates machine translation (MT) between Myanmar Sign Language (MSL) glosses and Myanmar Written Language (MWL). The MT models for both directions, MSL→MWL and MWL→MSL, are implemented by fine-tuning multilingual pre-trained language models, namely the mT5 and mBART-50 models. Subsequently, three techniques are employed to address the challenges posed to MT for these extremely low-resource languages. First, transfer learning is applied. The MT model is trained on a large-scale parallel corpus of American Sign Language and English and then re-trained using a small parallel corpus of MSL and MWL. Second, a self-training approach is employed. The translation pairs of MSL and MWL are created by translating sentences in a monolingual MWL corpus using the initially trained MT model. The synthetic and original MSL–MWL parallel corpora are then used to train the final MT model. Third, grammatical errors are corrected after the translation to enhance the quality of the translated sentences. An error correction model is obtained by fine-tuning the mT5 model using synthetic noisy data, which is automatically constructed by adding perturbations to the sentences in a monolingual MWL corpus. The experimental results show that each component of the proposed method contributes to improving the performance of MT between MSL and MWL. Furthermore, a comparative analysis is conducted on four token segmentation schemes, which are used as a preprocessing step in MT. 1

background.en: The paper addresses the challenge of machine translation between Myanmar Sign Language glosses and Myanmar Written Language. Sign language translation is critical yet extremely difficult due to a severe scarcity of parallel data, classifying these as extremely low-resource languages.
background.id: Makalah ini membahas tantangan *machine translation* antara *gloss* *Myanmar Sign Language* dan *Myanmar Written Language*. Penerjemahan bahasa isyarat sangat penting namun sangat sulit karena kelangkaan data paralel yang parah, yang menggolongkan bahasa-bahasa ini sebagai bahasa yang sangat *low-resource*.

contributions.en: The study introduces a comprehensive framework for bidirectional translation between Myanmar Sign Language and Myanmar Written Language. The main contributions include the application of transfer learning from American Sign Language and English data, a self-training approach using monolingual data, a post-translation error correction model, and a comparative analysis of four token segmentation schemes.
contributions.id: Studi ini memperkenalkan kerangka kerja komprehensif untuk penerjemahan dua arah antara *Myanmar Sign Language* dan *Myanmar Written Language*. Kontribusi utamanya meliputi penerapan *transfer learning* dari data *American Sign Language* dan bahasa Inggris, pendekatan *self-training* menggunakan data monolingual, model koreksi kesalahan pasca-penerjemahan, dan analisis komparatif dari empat skema *token segmentation*.

method.en: The authors implement machine translation models by fine-tuning multilingual pre-trained language models, specifically mT5 and mBART-50. To overcome resource scarcity, they apply transfer learning using American Sign Language and English parallel corpora before training on Myanmar Sign Language and Myanmar Written Language data. Additionally, they utilize self-training with synthetic pairs generated from monolingual text and apply an error correction model trained on synthetic noisy data. Four token segmentation schemes are also evaluated as part of preprocessing.
method.id: Para penulis mengimplementasikan model *machine translation* dengan melakukan *fine-tuning* pada *multilingual pre-trained language models*, khususnya mT5 dan mBART-50. Untuk mengatasi kelangkaan sumber daya, mereka menerapkan *transfer learning* menggunakan korpus paralel *American Sign Language* dan bahasa Inggris sebelum dilatih pada data *Myanmar Sign Language* dan *Myanmar Written Language*. Selain itu, mereka menggunakan *self-training* dengan pasangan sintetik yang dihasilkan dari teks monolingual dan menerapkan model koreksi kesalahan yang dilatih pada data bising sintetik. Empat skema *token segmentation* juga dievaluasi sebagai bagian dari *preprocessing*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.

results.en: Experimental results demonstrate that each proposed component, including transfer learning, self-training, and error correction, contributes positively to improving the translation performance between Myanmar Sign Language and Myanmar Written Language.
results.id: Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa setiap komponen yang diusulkan, termasuk *transfer learning*, *self-training*, dan koreksi kesalahan, memberikan kontribusi positif dalam meningkatkan kinerja penerjemahan antara *Myanmar Sign Language* dan *Myanmar Written Language*.

tldr.en: This paper investigates machine translation between Myanmar Sign Language glosses and Myanmar Written Language using fine-tuned multilingual pre-trained language models. The results show that transfer learning, self-training, and error correction significantly improve translation performance for these extremely low-resource settings.
tldr.id: Artikel ini menyelidiki *machine translation* antara *gloss* *Myanmar Sign Language* dan *Myanmar Written Language* menggunakan *multilingual pre-trained language models* yang di-*fine-tune*. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa *transfer learning*, *self-training*, dan koreksi kesalahan secara signifikan meningkatkan kinerja penerjemahan untuk pengaturan yang sangat *low-resource* ini.

doi:10.1145/3839365.abstract: Despite remarkable progress in large language models, Urdua language spoken by over 230 million people remains critically underrepresented in modern NLP systems. Existing multilingual models demonstrate poor performance on Urdu-specific tasks, struggling with the language’s complex morphology, right-to-left Nastaliq script, and rich literary traditions. Even the base LLaMA-3.1 8B-Instruct model shows limited capability in generating fluent, contextually appropriate Urdu text. We introduce Qalb, an Urdu language model developed through a two-stage approach: continued pre-training followed by supervised fine-tuning. Starting from LLaMA 3.1 8B, we perform continued pre-training on a dataset of 1.97 billion tokens. This corpus comprises 1.84 billion tokens of diverse Urdu text spanning news archives, classical and contemporary literature, government documents, and social media combined with 140 million tokens of English Wikipedia data to prevent catastrophic forgetting. We then fine-tune the resulting model on the Alif Urdu-instruct dataset. Through extensive evaluation on Urdu-specific benchmarks, Qalb demonstrates substantial improvements, achieving a weighted average score of 90.34 and out-performing the previous state-of-the-art Alif-1.0-Instruct model (87.1) by 3.24 points, while also surpassing the base LLaMA- 3.1 8B-Instruct model by 44.64 points. Qalb achieves state-of-the-art performance with comprehensive evaluation across seven diverse tasks including Classification, Sentiment Analysis, and Reasoning. Our results demonstrate that continued pre-training on diverse, high-quality language data, combined with targeted instruction fine-tuning, effectively adapts foundation models to low-resource languages.
doi:10.1145/3839365.journal_ref: ACM Transactions on Asian and Low-Resource Language Information Processing

glossary.explanation_id: Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada model bahasa yang sudah ada menggunakan *korpus* *data* tambahan untuk menguasai bahasa atau domain baru.
Tahap pelatihan di mana model dilatih menggunakan *dataset* ter-*anotasi* untuk mengikuti instruksi dan tugas tertentu dengan lebih baik.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa hanya memiliki sedikit *data* teks digital dan sumber daya komputasi yang tersedia untuk *NLP*.
Fenomena hilangnya kemampuan atau pengetahuan sebelumnya pada model ketika mempelajari *data* atau tugas baru.
Unit potongan teks terkecil yang diproses oleh *tokenizer* dalam model bahasa.

background.en: Despite remarkable progress in large language models, the Urdu language spoken by over 230 million people remains critically underrepresented in modern NLP systems. Existing multilingual models demonstrate poor performance on Urdu-specific tasks, struggling with the language's complex morphology, right-to-left Nastaliq script, and rich literary traditions. Even the base LLaMA-3.1 8B-Instruct model shows limited capability in generating fluent, contextually appropriate Urdu text, highlighting the urgent need for dedicated linguistic adaptation.
background.id: Meskipun ada kemajuan luar biasa dalam *large language model*, bahasa Urdu yang dituturkan oleh lebih dari 230 juta orang masih sangat kurang terwakili dalam sistem *NLP* modern. Model *multilingual* yang ada menunjukkan performa yang buruk pada tugas spesifik bahasa Urdu, kesulitan dengan morfologi bahasa yang kompleks, aksrip Nastaliq dari kanan ke kiri, serta tradisi sastra yang kaya. Bahkan model dasar LLaMA-3.1 8B-Instruct menunjukkan kemampuan yang terbatas dalam menghasilkan teks bahasa Urdu yang fasih dan sesuai konteks, yang menyoroti kebutuhan mendesak akan adaptasi linguistik khusus.

contributions.en: The authors introduce Qalb, the largest state-of-the-art Urdu large language model designed for 230 million speakers. The key novelty lies in the systematic two-stage approach combining continued pre-training on a large diverse Urdu corpus with targeted instruction fine-tuning.
contributions.id: Para penulis memperkenalkan Qalb, *large language model* bahasa Urdu *state-of-the-art* terbesar yang dirancang untuk 230 juta penutur. Kebaruan utama terletak pada pendekatan dua tahap yang sistematis yang menggabungkan *continued pre-training* pada *korpus* bahasa Urdu yang besar dan beragam dengan *instruction fine-tuning* yang ditargetkan.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail, though it concludes that continued pre-training on diverse high-quality data combined with targeted instruction fine-tuning effectively adapts foundation models to low-resource languages.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan secara rinci, meskipun menyimpulkan bahwa *continued pre-training* pada *data* berkualitas tinggi yang beragam yang dikombinasikan dengan *instruction fine-tuning* yang ditargetkan secara efektif mengadaptasi model fondasi ke bahasa *low-resource*.

method.en: The development of Qalb follows a two-stage approach consisting of continued pre-training followed by supervised fine-tuning. Starting from the LLaMA 3.1 8B model, the authors perform continued pre-training on a dataset of 1.97 billion tokens, which combines 1.84 billion tokens of diverse Urdu text from news, literature, government documents, and social media, along with 140 million tokens of English Wikipedia data to prevent catastrophic forgetting. Subsequently, the resulting model is fine-tuned on the Alif Urdu-instruct dataset and evaluated across seven diverse tasks including classification, sentiment analysis, and reasoning.
method.id: Pengembangan Qalb mengikuti pendekatan dua tahap yang terdiri dari *continued pre-training* yang diikuti oleh *supervised fine-tuning*. Dimulai dari model LLaMA 3.1 8B, para penulis melakukan *continued pre-training* pada *dataset* sebesar 1,97 miliar *token*, yang menggabungkan 1,84 miliar *token* teks bahasa Urdu yang beragam dari berita, sastra, dokumen pemerintah, dan media sosial, beserta 140 juta *token* *data* Wikipedia bahasa Inggris untuk mencegah *catastrophic forgetting*. Selanjutnya, model yang dihasilkan di-*fine-tune* pada *dataset* Alif Urdu-instruct dan dievaluasi pada tujuh tugas yang beragam termasuk klasifikasi, analisis sentimen, dan penalaran.

related_work.en: The paper compares Qalb against previous state-of-the-art models such as Alif-1.0-Instruct and the base LLaMA-3.1 8B-Instruct model, noting that existing multilingual and baseline systems struggle to capture the complex morphology and script characteristics of Urdu.
related_work.id: Makalah ini membandingkan Qalb dengan model *state-of-the-art* sebelumnya seperti Alif-1.0-Instruct dan model dasar LLaMA-3.1 8B-Instruct, serta mencatat bahwa sistem *multilingual* dan *baseline* yang ada kesulitan menangkap morfologi yang kompleks dan karakteristik aksara bahasa Urdu.

results.en: Through extensive evaluation on Urdu-specific benchmarks, Qalb achieves a weighted average score of 90.34. It outperforms the previous state-of-the-art Alif-1.0-Instruct model by 3.24 points and surpasses the base LLaMA-3.1 8B-Instruct model by 44.64 points, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance across seven diverse tasks such as classification, sentiment analysis, and reasoning.
results.id: Melalui *evaluasi* ekstensif pada *benchmark* khusus bahasa Urdu, Qalb mencapai skor rata-rata tertimbang sebesar 90,34. Model ini mengungguli model *state-of-the-art* sebelumnya Alif-1.0-Instruct sebesar 3,24 poin dan melampaui model dasar LLaMA-3.1 8B-Instruct sebesar 44,64 poin, menunjukkan performa *state-of-the-art* di tujuh tugas yang beragam seperti klasifikasi, analisis sentimen, dan penalaran.

tldr.en: We introduce Qalb, a large language model tailored for Urdu through continued pre-training and supervised fine-tuning. Qalb achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse Urdu NLP tasks, outperforming existing baseline models.
tldr.id: Kami memperkenalkan Qalb, sebuah *large language model* yang disesuaikan untuk bahasa Urdu melalui *continued pre-training* dan *supervised fine-tuning*. Qalb mencapai performa *state-of-the-art* pada berbagai tugas *NLP* bahasa Urdu, mengungguli model *baseline* yang ada.

doi:10.1145/3839451.abstract: Modern software systems routinely invoke components whose source code is unavailable, such as proprietary libraries or cloud-based APIs. Such closed-box functions provide only oracle-style access: they can be executed on concrete inputs, but their internal logic cannot be inspected. Prior work has explored augmenting SMT solvers—the foundational engines behind contemporary automated reasoning—to handle satisfiability queries over first-order formulas containing calls to such closed-box functions. However, these approaches primarily rely on testing-based techniques to search for satisfying models and therefore do not support constructing proofs of unsatisfiability. While model search is sufficient for bug-finding tasks, the inability to generate unsatisfiability proofs fundamentally limits their applicability to formal verification. In this work, we present the first SMT solver capable of producing proofs of unsatisfiability for first-order theories that include closed-box function calls. Our key insight is to leverage large language models (LLMs) to conjecture auxiliary lemmas—based on natural language documentation of the closed-box functions—that capture properties relevant for reasoning about their behavior. To support this approach, we introduce an extension of the SMT-LIB language that allows the declaration of closed-box functions together with natural language descriptions, usage documentation, examples, and oracle interfaces. We, then, develop NLUnsat, an SMT solver that operates over this extended syntax to find unsatisfiability proofs on SMT-LIB formulas with closed-box functions. On a benchmark suite of 193 extended SMT-LIB problems involving closed-box functions, NLUnsat equipped with the openai.gpt-oss:20b LLM solves 89% of the instances, and a virtual best solver across five LLMs solves 98% of the instances. We further evaluate NLUnsat in the setting of deductive verification for programs containing closed-box function calls. On a collection of 15 benchmark programs, our verifier, using NLUnsat as its backend solver, successfully proves all verification goals when given access to a pool of two LLMs, openai.gpt-oss:20b and openai.gpt-oss:120b. Finally, we evaluate NLUnsat on satisfiable benchmark instances: none of these instances were incorrectly classified as unsatisfiable, and the solver successfully finds models for 57 out of 107 satisfiable instances.

contributions.en: This work presents the first SMT solver capable of producing proofs of unsatisfiability for first-order theories that include closed-box function calls. The key novelty lies in leveraging large language models to conjecture auxiliary lemmas derived from natural language documentation to reason about closed-box behaviors, alongside an extension of the SMT-LIB language for declaring such functions.

Kebaruan utamanya terletak pada pemanfaatan *large language model* untuk menduga lema tambahan yang diturunkan dari dokumentasi bahasa alami guna menalar perilaku kotak hitam, beserta ekstensi bahasa *SMT-LIB* untuk mendeklarasikan fungsi tersebut.

method.en: The approach introduces an extension to the SMT-LIB language allowing the declaration of closed-box functions together with natural language descriptions, usage documentation, examples, and oracle interfaces. However, these existing approaches rely primarily on testing-based techniques to search for satisfying models, which restricts their utility since they cannot support constructing proofs of unsatisfiability.
related_work.id: Pekerjaan sebelumnya telah mengeksplorasi penambahan *SMT solver* untuk menangani kueri *satisfiability* pada rumus tingkat pertama yang berisi panggilan ke fungsi kotak hitam. Namun, pendekatan yang ada ini terutama mengandalkan teknik berbasis pengujian untuk mencari model yang memenuhi, yang membatasi kegunaannya karena tidak dapat mendukung pembangunan bukti *unsatisfiability*.

results.en: Evaluated on a benchmark suite of 193 extended SMT-LIB problems, NLUnsat using the openai.gpt-oss:20b model solves 89 percent of instances, while a virtual best solver across five LLMs solves 98 percent. tldr.en: This paper introduces NLUnsat, an SMT solver that utilizes large language models to generate proofs of unsatisfiability for first-order theories involving closed-box functions. The evaluation demonstrates that NLUnsat successfully solves 89 percent of benchmark instances using a single LLM and achieves higher performance with a multi-LLM configuration.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan NLUnsat, sebuah *SMT solver* yang memanfaatkan *large language model* untuk menghasilkan bukti *unsatisfiability* untuk teori tingkat pertama yang melibatkan fungsi kotak hitam. Evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa NLUnsat berhasil menyelesaikan 89 persen instans *benchmark* menggunakan satu *LLM* dan mencapai performa lebih tinggi dengan konfigurasi multi-*LLM*.

doi:10.1145/3845610.abstract: Dialogue tasks in low-resource languages face numerous challenges. Directly applying Large Language Models (LLMs) for response generation often leads to issues such as grammatical errors or hallucinations. Dialogue Response Selection (DRS), which selects responses from a predefined corpus, offers a more reliable alternative by reducing such risks. However, in extremely low-resource scenarios, limited retrieval capabilities and the lack of training data present significant challenges for practical implementation. To address this, this study proposes a two-stage DRS-based framework for dialogue systems in Taiwanese Indigenous languages. The first stage uses On-the-fly Translation to convert user inputs from low-resource languages into Chinese, leveraging a high-resource language as a pivot to improve retrieval accuracy. In the second stage, response candidates are retrieved based on the translated input and ranked by an LLM serving as the response selector, eliminating the need for additional model fine-tuning. To support evaluation under low-resource constraints, we also construct a simulated user input dataset and propose LaRQ (LLM-guided Response Quality Evaluation), an automated metric shown to align closely with human judgments. Overall, our method improves LaRQ over the no-pivot baseline by about 0.3 on average and up to 0.44 across models, demonstrating the effectiveness of pivot-language translation and LLM-based selection in enhancing dialogue quality for low-resource languages.

doi:10.11591/edulearn.v20i4.26450.abstract: The Philippine education sector increasingly relies on printed, digital, and blended modules to sustain and personalize learning. This quantitative experimental study compared these delivery formats in the subject language and communication in Filipino academic contex among 108 randomly selected grade 11 learners assigned to printed-only, digital-only, or blended (print+digital) conditions. A validated researcher-made 50-item achievement test was administered before and after a six-week intervention in which groups studied the same competencies and completed parallel tasks, differing only in delivery format. Using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to control baseline performance, posttest scores differed significantly by modality, F(2, 104)=18.91, p0.001, partial η²=0.27. The blended group obtained the highest mean score (M=42.78) and significantly outperformed both single-format groups, while printed-only and digital-only outcomes were comparable. Open-ended feedback suggested that print resources supported organization and annotation, whereas digital activities enabled practice and timely feedback; combining both helped clarify steps and correct errors. Consistent with constructivism and the cognitive theory of multimedia learning, intentionally integrated print and digital components appear to enhance interactivity and manage cognitive load. Schools are encouraged to adopt accessible blended module designs and provide implementation support in low-connectivity contexts; future studies should replicate the comparison in other settings and examine longer-term retention.

tldr.en: This study compares printed, digital, and blended learning modules among grade 11 learners in a Filipino subject. The results show that the blended format significantly outperforms single-format delivery.

doi:10.11591/eei.v15i4.11431.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems have achieved significant progress in recent years; however, their performance remains limited for low-resource languages such as Indonesian. Multilingual ASR models are often expected to generalize across languages, yet they frequently underperform when applied to underrepresented languages without sufficient adaptation. This study presents a comparative evaluation of three ASR models—Wav2Vec 2.0, XLS-R, and XLSR-53—on Indonesian speech to analyze the impact of monolingual fine-tuning versus multilingual pretraining. The evaluation was conducted using approximately 28 hours of validated Indonesian speech from the Common Voice Corpus version 13. Model performance was assessed using word error rate (WER) without employing any external language model to ensure a fair comparison. Experimental results demonstrate that Wav2Vec 2.0, which is fine-tuned specifically for Indonesian, achieves substantially lower WER compared to the multilingual models. Qualitative analysis further confirms that multilingual models exhibit higher omission and substitution errors. These findings indicate that language-specific fine-tuning plays a more critical role than multilingual generalization in achieving accurate ASR for Indonesian. The results provide practical guidance for deploying ASR systems in low-resource language scenarios and highlight the importance of targeted model adaptation.
